title: Network-Offloaded Bandwidth-Optimal Broadcast and Allgather for Distributed AI
problem: In FSDP training with interleaved collective operations, Allgather and Reduce-Scatter compete for injection bandwidth, creating pipeline bubbles that reduce communication/computation overlap efficiency.
motivation: Collective communication is a critical bottleneck in distributed AI training at scale, limiting performance and efficiency of large-scale model training.
method: The approach uses hardware multicast—a network feature that broadcasts data to multiple machines simultaneously—to create an efficient broadcast protocol that works in constant time regardless of how many computers participate. This broadcast becomes the foundation for scheduling Allgather operations (gathering data from all computers) in a way that fully saturates available network bandwidth. Instead of burdening the main CPU with coordination, the algorithm runs on a SmartNIC (a specialized network card), eliminating CPU overhead and enabling multiple data movements to happen in parallel.
key_novelty: Using hardware multicast to build bandwidth-optimal Allgather operations with execution offloaded to a SmartNIC (specialized network card) so the main CPU stays free.
contributions: Bandwidth-optimal Allgather algorithm achieving 2x traffic reduction
SmartNIC-offloaded collective operations engine freeing host resources
Demonstrated scalability to 1.6 Tbit/s network links on 188-node cluster

metrics.other: 2x traffic reduction on 188-node testbed, scalable to 1.6 Tbit/s link speeds
